SMTO-AUT-0027 — The Google sign-in took too long

GUID: 57a741b1-ac69-5172-a967-4adac381acc6
Slug: google-authorization-timeout
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • Each Google sign-in link from SMTO works for only 10 minutes, and this one ran past that before Google sent you back. SMTO saved nothing from it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to connect your Google account again to get a new sign-in link. The old link's request has expired and can't be reused.
  2. Before opening the link, have your Google password and any 2-Step Verification phone or key ready. Being ready helps you get through all of Google's screens inside the 10-minute window.
  3. Open the new link right away, sign in with the Google account you intend to use, and continue until the page says you're connected. SMTO only accepts Google's answer while the request behind that link is still active.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in tab says your email is connected and you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the sign-in link or anything from Google's address bar into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Google browser callback matched a pending authorization that had already passed its 10-minute lifetime, so the code was not exchanged.

What this means

  • The shared browser flow found the matched pending transaction beyond its ten-minute lifetime before exchanging the code. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The shared browser flow found the matched pending transaction beyond its ten-minute lifetime before exchanging the code.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the current pending request's expiry with the callback; an already removed transaction may instead report invalid state.

How to fix it

  • Restart consent with auth.google_connect and complete it within 600 seconds; BrowserOAuth pending transactions are single-use and expire after ten minutes. If users regularly run out of time, check for slow redirects or proxies delaying the callback to SMTO.
  • Restart auth.google_connect and complete consent within ten minutes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh matching consent response arrives before its transaction expires.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
